96daf0b6095c65fa.heading: Limit on Income Tax reliefs (Self Assessment helpsheet HS204)

amounts.name: Limit on Income Tax reliefs
amounts.period: 2025 to 2026 and later years (originally from 6 April 2013)
amounts.value: £50,000, or 25% of adjusted total income if higher

amounts.name: Adjusted total income threshold for needing to calculate the limit

caveats: This version (HS204 2026) explains the limit for 2025 to 2026 and later years; earlier years may have different specific box references.
Under Making Tax Digital for Income Tax, claims and adjustments will be made via software rather than the SA boxes listed, so the box references may not apply to all taxpayers going forward.

The limit does not affect trading losses used against capital gains, or losses used against profits of the same trade/property business, or EIS/SEIS share loss relief - these are excluded from the calculation.
Loan interest relief that cannot be given in full due to the limit cannot be carried forward as a trade loss, unlike certain other excess loan interest for partnership trades.

definitions.meaning: Figure calculated (via Working Sheet 1) used to determine 25% relief limit when total income exceeds £200,000

Trade loss relief against general income and early trade losses relief, property loss relief (capital allowances/agricultural expenses), post-cessation trade/property relief, employment loss relief, former employees deduction for liabilities, losses on deeply discounted securities and strips of government securities, share loss relief (except EIS/SEIS), and qualifying loan interest

obligations.must: Restrict aggregate relief claimed against total income to the greater of £50,000 or 25% of adjusted total income
obligations.trigger: Total relevant reliefs claimed against general income exceed £50,000 in a tax year
obligations.who: Individual claiming trade loss relief, property loss relief, post-cessation reliefs, employment loss relief, losses on deeply discounted securities, share loss relief, or qualifying loan interest against general income

obligations.must: Calculate adjusted total income using Working Sheet 1 to determine the revised limit
obligations.who: Individual with total income over £200,000 claiming affected reliefs

obligations.must: Make claims and adjustments through compatible software instead of Self Assessment boxes
obligations.trigger: Required to use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax
obligations.who: Individual using Making Tax Digital for Income Tax with self-employment or property income

note.summary: HS204 explains the cap on certain Income Tax reliefs (trade loss relief, property loss relief, post-cessation reliefs, employment loss relief, losses on deeply discounted securities, share loss relief, qualifying loan interest) that can be set against total income, applicable from 6 April 2013: the greater of £50,000 or 25% of adjusted total income. It identifies the specific SA return boxes affected (SA103S, SA103F, SA103L, SA104S, SA104F, SA105, SA106, SA101, SA108), gives worked examples of how the limit and ordering of relief claims operate, lists exceptions (e.g. losses against profits of the same trade/property business, EIS/SEIS share loss relief), and notes that adjusted total income only needs calculating if total income exceeds £200,000. It also flags that under Making Tax Digital for Income Tax, claims will be made through compatible software rather than SA return boxes.
